artiest/san-francisco-symphony.text:
The San Francisco Symphony is an American orchestra from San Francisco. It was founded in 1911 and began with sixty musicians under the leadership of Henry Kimball Hadley. Since 1980 it has played in Louise M. Davies Symphony Hall. In 1926 the orchestra was the first to broadcast symphonic concerts on the radio, and those broadcasts continued for more than thirty years.

In the 1930s the orchestra was almost bankrupted by the Depression. The 1934–35 season was cancelled and the residents of the city voted for public funding. Pierre Monteux then rebuilt the orchestra and in 1941 a new recording contract with RCA Victor followed. Josef Krips became music director in 1963 and brought strict discipline, especially in the German-Austrian repertoire. Seiji Ozawa followed in 1970 and had Deutsche Grammophon record the orchestra, among other things with the Symphonic Dances from West Side Story by Leonard Bernstein. Later music directors were Edo de Waart, Herbert Blomstedt and Michael Tilson Thomas, who from 1995 became the longest-serving music director. After him came Esa-Pekka Salonen and Elim Chan.

The orchestra plays the classical-romantic repertoire, but also a great deal of American music, especially under Ozawa and Tilson Thomas. It recorded for labels including Deutsche Grammophon, Philips and RCA and later for its own label, SFS Media. The recordings show how an American orchestra developed into a world-class ensemble in the twentieth century.
artiest/san-francisco-symphony.listen: Listen to the Symphonic Dances from West Side Story by Leonard Bernstein. Notice the Latin American rhythms and the fierce percussion, and how well the orchestra holds on to the swing of the dance.

artiest/santana.text:
Santana is an American rock band from San Francisco, founded in 1966 by the Mexican-American guitarist Carlos Santana. That year he discovered the city's hippie movement and set up a group of his own. In 1967 the band was given an audition with the concert promoter Bill Graham at the Fillmore Auditorium, and at the end of 1968 a contract with Columbia Records followed. Carlos Santana is the only constant member through all the line-ups.

The breakthrough came in August 1969 with a performance at Woodstock. The debut album Santana appeared shortly afterwards, with Evil Ways among others. Then followed Abraxas (1970), with a reworking of Black Magic Woman by Fleetwood Mac, Oye Como Va and the instrumental Samba Pa Ti, and Santana III in 1971. These albums were made by the classic line-up with Gregg Rolie on organ and vocals, the percussionists Michael Carabello and José Chepito Areas, the drummer Michael Shrieve and the bassist David Brown. Producer Graham had advised the group to shorten the long jams and make real songs.

The sound of Santana mixes rock and blues with Afro-Cuban rhythms and jazz. Besides the electric guitar, organ and full percussion are defining. From 1972 the band chose jazz fusion, on Caravanserai, Welcome and Borboletta. It reached a new peak in 1999 with Supernatural, which included Smooth among others. The classic line-up later came together again for Santana IV in 2016. Santana showed that Latin American percussion can take a central place in rock music.
artiest/santana.listen: Listen to Samba Pa Ti and follow only the guitar. Notice how the tone sustains and sings, as if it were a voice, while the percussion beneath keeps a soft Latin rhythm.

artiest/santo-en-johnny.text:
Santo & Johnny was an American instrumental duo of Italian descent from Brooklyn, New York. The brothers Santo Farina, born in 1937, and Johnny Farina, born in 1941, grew up in a family where their father wanted the boys to learn the steel guitar. Santo began on that instrument at a young age and was already writing his own pieces at fourteen. Johnny later accompanied him on an ordinary electric guitar. When Johnny was sixteen, they left school to start a music career.

Their first single, Sleep Walk, came out in 1959, recorded in Manhattan and released on Canadian-American Records. In September of that year the single spent two weeks at the top of the Billboard chart. It was one of the few instrumentals of the rock era to manage that. The follow-up Tear Drop was also successful. Later they made another version of In the Still of the Night, which in 1964 became their last American hit. In Europe and Mexico they remained popular. In Italy they even got a television show of their own.

The music revolves around the soft, singing sound of the steel guitar, accompanied by Johnny's electric guitar. The melodies are calm and almost dreamy. Sleep Walk is still played a great deal and used in commercials, television programmes and films. The duo split up in 1976 and was inducted into the Steel Guitar Hall of Fame in 2002. Santo stopped making music, Johnny kept performing.
artiest/santo-en-johnny.listen: Listen to Sleep Walk and notice how the steel guitar lets the melody glide from note to note, while the second guitar quietly lays chords beneath it.

artiest/sapna-awasthi.text:
Sapna Awasthi, also known as Sapna Awasthi Singh, is an Indian playback singer who sings for Bollywood films. As a child she began studying classical music and earned the Sangeet Vishaarad diploma at the Bhatkhande Music Institute in Lucknow. At fifteen she sang on the radio, and then on stage as well. She got her first chance in the film world from the composer Sameer Sen.

She comes from the Kumaon region in Uttarakhand and moved to Mumbai after singing songs for the 1994 film Krantiveer. There she worked for well-known film composers, including Nadeem Shravan, Anand Milind, Anu Malik and A. R. Rahman. Her best-known songs are Banno Teri Ankhiyan Soorme from Dushmani (1995), Pardesi Pardesi from Raja Hindustani (1996), Chaiyya Chaiyya from Dil Se (1998) and Angoori Badan from Jaanwar (1998). She sang Chaiyya Chaiyya together with Sukhvinder Singh for the music of Rahman. Pardesi Pardesi, a duet with Udit Narayan and Alka Yagnik, is, according to the source, usually regarded as her biggest hit.

In Hindi film music the actor does not sing himself or herself; a playback singer, recorded in advance in the studio, does. Anyone who saw a Bollywood film in the 1990s has therefore probably heard her voice, even though her name was not on the poster.
artiest/sapna-awasthi.listen: Listen to Chaiyya Chaiyya from Dil Se and notice the interplay between her voice and that of Sukhvinder Singh above the tight, rhythmic percussion of the accompaniment.

artiest/sarah-mclachlan.text:
Sarah McLachlan is a Canadian singer-songwriter, born in 1968 in Halifax, Nova Scotia. She grew up as the youngest of three adopted children and studied classical guitar, piano, voice and opera for twelve years. At seventeen she sang in the rock band The October Game. After a performance in Halifax she was offered a contract by Nettwerk Records, the Vancouver label to which she moved. Terry McBride, co-founder of the label, became her manager.

Her debut album Touch was released in 1988. Solace from 1991 brought the breakthrough in Canada and marked the start of her collaboration with the producer Pierre Marchand. Fumbling Towards Ecstasy from 1993 made her known internationally as well. Nettwerk did not rely on radio, but on relentless touring, and she was on stage almost without a break. With Surfacing in 1997 she had her greatest success, with Building a Mystery, Last Dance and Angel among others. With it she won two Grammy Awards and four Juno Awards.

Angel, written after the death of the Smashing Pumpkins keyboardist Jonathan Melvoin, became a song about grief and consolation and was heard in the film City of Angels. Her music is calm and melodic, with a clear, sensitive voice, piano and acoustic guitar, and lyrics about longing, loss and recovery. She was inducted into the Canadian Music Hall of Fame. She showed that a singer with understated songs can reach the whole world.
artiest/sarah-mclachlan.listen: Listen to Angel from Surfacing and notice how little happens: a piano, a muted accompaniment and her voice, which begins softly and slowly opens up.

artiest/sarah-vaughan.text: Sarah Vaughan from Newark won a talent contest at the Apollo Theater in 1942. She sang in Earl Hines's big band, in which Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker also played, and later named those two as her most important teachers. She took the harmony and the lines of bebop into her singing. In 1945 she made Lover Man with Gillespie and Parker. Her voice had an enormous range, from deep to very high, and she could make it sound like an instrument. Her nickname was 'Sassy' or 'The Divine One'. Her 1954 album with the trumpeter Clifford Brown is regarded as a high point. She kept performing until the late 1980s.
artiest/sarah-vaughan.listen: Hear how she makes big leaps and embellishes the melody with harmonies.

artiest/sathima-bea-benjamin.text:
Sathima Bea Benjamin was a South African singer and composer. She was born in 1936 in Claremont, Cape Town, and sang as a teenager at talent contests in the cinema. In the 1950s she performed in nightclubs and at dances with Cape pianists. Her singing style, with light phrasing and clear diction, was shaped by Nat King Cole, Billie Holiday, Doris Day and Ella Fitzgerald, whom she knew from the radio. In 1959 she met the pianist Dollar Brand, later known as Abdullah Ibrahim, in Cape Town, and married him in 1965.

After the Sharpeville massacre in 1960 they left South Africa and settled in Zurich. In 1963 she met Duke Ellington, who had her sing and had the couple flown to Paris to record for the label Reprise. Her recording remained unreleased for a long time and appeared only in 1996 as A Morning in Paris. In 1965 she sang Solitude with Ellington's orchestra at the Newport Jazz Festival.

In 1976 she recorded African Songbird in South Africa, after which the family moved to New York. In 1979 she founded the label Ekapa, on which she released eight albums, including Dedications, WindSong, LoveLight and Musical Echoes. Dedications received a Grammy nomination in 1982. She worked with American jazz musicians in New York and with South African musicians in Cape Town. She died in 2013. Her work links the jazz standards of Ellington with the voice of Cape Town.
artiest/sathima-bea-benjamin.listen: Listen to A Morning in Paris and notice her light, clear way of singing: she does not use many ornaments, but puts the emphasis on the words and the phrasing.

artiest/satyajit-ray.text: Satyajit Ray (1921–1992) from Kolkata is best known as a film director. For his first films he worked with musicians from Indian classical music: Ravi Shankar, Vilayat Khan and Ali Akbar Khan. Ray noticed that their first loyalty lay with the musical tradition and not with his film. From Teen Kanya (1961) onwards he therefore wrote his film music himself. He was a connoisseur of Western classical music, and Beethoven was his favourite composer. He wanted to use Western forms mainly in films set in the city. In this way he wrote the music for Charulata (1964) and Aranyer Din Ratri (1970). For the fairy-tale film Goopy Gyne Bagha Byne (1969) he also wrote the songs.
artiest/satyajit-ray.listen: Listen to how Ray uses a small ensemble to make short, clear themes that belong to a character, such as the theme of Charu, and how Indian instruments and Western harmony go together.

artiest/sayeeduddin-dagar.text:
Hussain Sayeeduddin Dagar, known among musicians as Saeed Bhai, was an Indian singer from the dhrupad tradition. Dhrupad is the oldest surviving form of North Indian classical music, Hindustani classical music. He was born in 1939 in Alwar in Rajasthan and died in 2017. He belonged to the Dagar family and was the nineteenth generation in that line. His cousins, among them the so-called Senior and Junior Dagar Brothers, were also famous dhrupad singers.

His father was Hussainuddin Khan Dagar, who died in 1963. At the age of six Sayeeduddin began to learn from him, later also from his uncle Rahimuddin Khan Dagar. He was president of the Dhrupad Society in Jaipur and in Pune and himself lived in Pune. He also appeared in the well-known Indian television series Bharat Ek Khoj.

Dhrupad sounds very different from pop music. It is slow, restrained and meditative, and a singer builds a raga from long, calm notes, often accompanied by a stringed instrument and a drum. Saeed Bhai belonged to the last representatives of a tradition handed down from father to son. His work shows where Indian classical music comes from.
artiest/sayeeduddin-dagar.listen: Listen to a recording of Sayeeduddin Dagar and notice the beginning: the singer takes his time for a long, slow build-up, without a fixed metre, before the rhythm enters.

artiest/schlippenbach-trio.text:
The Schlippenbach Trio is a European free jazz group around the German pianist Alexander von Schlippenbach. Playing with him are the saxophonist Evan Parker and the percussionist Paul Lovens. Their best-known early record is Pakistani Pomade, recorded in 1972 in Germany for the label FMP. The record contains pieces such as Moonbeef and Ein Husten für Karl Valentin, which were written by all three musicians together. There is thus no leader who devises the music: the three improvise and compose together.

The trio's music revolves around colour, texture and density, in both sound and harmony. Reviewers praised the record for the taste and the elegance of a group that gave free improvisation in Europe a face of its own. The Penguin Guide to Jazz gave Pakistani Pomade a Crown, a distinction for recordings for which the authors have a special admiration.

The trio stayed together for decades and later made many more recordings, such as Elf Bagatellen in 1991, Gold Is Where You Find It in 2008 and Features in 2015. It is a good example of European improvised music, which in the 1970s broke away from the American model.
artiest/schlippenbach-trio.listen: Listen to Pakistani Pomade and try to follow the three voices: piano, saxophone and percussion do not take turns at a solo, but react to each other continually.

artiest/schonberg-ensemble.text:
The Schönberg Ensemble was a Dutch ensemble for contemporary classical music. It was founded in 1974 by students and former students of the Royal Conservatoire in The Hague and existed until 2009. The conductor was Reinbert de Leeuw. The ensemble was named after Arnold Schönberg, and its first repertoire consisted accordingly only of chamber music by the composers of the Second Viennese School. Later it expanded to cover the whole of the twentieth century and the twenty-first.

The regular line-up consisted of mostly single-desk woodwinds, brass, piano, percussion, harp and strings. The combinations varied for each programme, because contemporary music often calls for unusual line-ups. If a larger ensemble was needed, it played together with the Asko Ensemble. Many Dutch and foreign composers wrote pieces especially for the group. It played in the Concertgebouw and other Dutch halls and toured almost all of Europe, but also Canada, the United States, India and Japan.

The ensemble made many recordings. The breadth shows in the list: Verklärte Nacht and Pierrot lunaire by Schönberg, De Staat, Des canyons aux étoiles... by Messiaen, choral works and the project The Ligeti Project. In 2008 it merged with the Asko Ensemble to form Asko|Schönberg, under the direction of Reinbert de Leeuw. Later the group changed its name to Het Muziek. The Schönberg Ensemble shows how the Netherlands won a place of its own in modern classical music in the late twentieth century.
artiest/schonberg-ensemble.listen: Listen to Pierrot lunaire by Schönberg in this ensemble's performance. Notice the small, constantly changing line-up and the way the voice shifts between singing and speaking.

artiest/schoolly-d.text:
Schoolly D, real name Jesse Bonds Weaver Jr., is an American rapper from Philadelphia. He was born in 1962 in West Philadelphia and also grew up in Georgia. In the mid-1980s he worked with DJ Code Money. His lyrics dealt with urban realism, violence and sexual bravado. The music was sparse and hard, with electronic, economical rhythms. His first records appeared in the 1980s, including Schoolly D, Saturday Night! The Album and Smoke Some Kill.

His song P.S.K. is often cited as one of the first records of what later came to be called gangsta rap. Ice-T described in his autobiography how that record influenced him in writing 6 in the Mornin'. For that reason Schoolly D is regarded as one of the inventors of the genre. Later he embraced an Afrocentric style and, together with KRS-One, brought Afrocentric culture into hip hop.

His music is also heard in films by the director Abel Ferrara, including King of New York and Bad Lieutenant. The song Signifying Rapper from Smoke Some Kill was removed from the soundtrack of Bad Lieutenant because Led Zeppelin won a lawsuit over an uncleared reference to Kashmir. He also wrote music for the animated series Aqua Teen Hunger Force. Schoolly D shows that hip hop was already finding a hard voice of its own in the streets of Philadelphia in the early 1980s.
artiest/schoolly-d.listen: Listen to P.S.K. or another early track and notice how bare the accompaniment is: a hard drum machine and above it a voice that almost speaks, without melody.

artiest/scorpions.text:
The Scorpions are a German hard rock and heavy metal band from Hanover. Guitarist Rudolf Schenker founded the group in 1965. Singer Klaus Meine has played in it since 1969. The best-known line-up, with Schenker, Meine, guitarist Matthias Jabs, bassist Francis Buchholz and drummer Herman Rarebell, existed from 1978 to 1992. The debut album Lonesome Crow appeared in 1972, with Schenker's younger brother Michael on guitar. He left for UFO and was replaced by Uli Jon Roth, who can be heard on Fly to the Rainbow, In Trance, Virgin Killer and the live album Tokyo Tapes, among others.

After Roth's departure the band brought in Jabs and moved towards a more melodic rock style, audible on Lovedrive from 1979. The album Love at First Sting from 1984 contains Rock You Like a Hurricane and Still Loving You, two songs that were highly influential. The biggest hit was Wind of Change, from the album Crazy World from 1990, a song that was seen as a symbol of the political changes in Eastern Europe and the fall of the Berlin Wall. The Scorpions were the first heavy metal band from a non-English-speaking country to have international success.

In August 1989 the band appeared at a large rock festival in Moscow, in the middle of the Cold War. For that reason it features in the course in the magazine on living with the bomb. Its music shows that rock could work as a bridge, also between East and West.
artiest/scorpions.listen: Listen to Wind of Change and notice the whistling at the beginning and the calm guitars beneath the vocals. Can you hear how this rock song sounds like a ballad, with a chorus to sing along to?

artiest/scott-joplin.text: Scott Joplin grew up in Texarkana and as a young pianist travelled around the Midwest. In Sedalia, Missouri, he played at the Maple Leaf Club and studied music at a college for Black students. In 1899 John Stark published his Maple Leaf Rag, which sold well for years and earned him the nickname 'King of Ragtime'. Joplin saw ragtime as serious music and wrote strict, elaborate pieces in it. He moved to New York and wrote the opera Treemonisha, which he never saw performed in full during his lifetime. In 1916 he still recorded a few piano rolls. He died in 1917. Thanks to the ragtime revival of the 1970s he became famous again, and in 1976 he was posthumously awarded a Pulitzer Prize.
artiest/scott-joplin.listen: Listen to the four sections of the rag and hear how each section brings a new melody.

artiest/scott-lafaro.text:
Scott LaFaro was an American jazz bassist, born in 1936 in Newark, New Jersey. He first played piano, bass clarinet and tenor saxophone, and began on the double bass only at eighteen, because a string instrument was compulsory for music education students. He played in Buddy Morrow's big band, in Los Angeles with Victor Feldman and Hampton Hawes and later with Chet Baker, Stan Kenton, Cal Tjader and Benny Goodman.

In 1959 he joined the pianist Bill Evans, who had just left Miles Davis's sextet. With Evans and the drummer Paul Motian he developed a countermelodic approach: the bass did not merely play a conventional walking bass, but held a conversation of its own with the piano. The trio saw itself as three equal voices that together work out one musical idea, often without any of them explicitly keeping time. In January 1961 he also took Charlie Haden's place with Ornette Coleman. On the last day of a two-week engagement at the Village Vanguard in June 1961 two albums were recorded: Sunday at the Village Vanguard and Waltz for Debby.

On 6 July 1961 LaFaro was killed in a car accident. He was twenty-five. Evans stopped performing for months. Although his career was short, LaFaro is regarded as one of the most influential bassists in jazz. His virtuosity and his countermelodies changed the idea of what a bass can do in a trio.
artiest/scott-lafaro.listen: Listen to Waltz for Debby by the Bill Evans Trio from the Village Vanguard and focus only on the double bass. Can you hear how the bass does not merely mark the chords, but makes melody itself and talks with the piano?

artiest/scott-mckenzie.text:
Scott McKenzie, real name Philip Wallach Blondheim III, was an American singer and songwriter. He was born in 1939 in Jacksonville, Florida, and grew up in North Carolina and Virginia. There he became friends with John Phillips. Together they formed doo-wop groups in the 1950s, which in New York came to be called the Smoothies and recorded singles for Decca. His stage name came about after a party following a show, when a comedian thought he looked like a Scottish terrier.

In 1961 Phillips and McKenzie formed the folk trio The Journeymen with Dick Weissman, which recorded three albums and seven singles for Capitol. After the success of The Beatles in 1964 the group stopped. Phillips founded The Mamas & the Papas. McKenzie first tried to make something of himself as a solo artist and signed with Lou Adler's label Ode Records.

Phillips wrote and produced San Francisco (Be Sure to Wear Some Flowers in Your Hair) for him, released in May 1967. The single was an instant hit, reached number four in the Billboard Hot 100 and topped the chart in Britain and more countries. The song, with its soft bell, calm guitar and Joe Osborn's bass, became the musical image of the Summer of Love. His album The Voice of Scott McKenzie followed, then Stained Glass Morning. In the early 1970s he stopped recording. He later co-wrote Kokomo for The Beach Boys. McKenzie died in 2012.
artiest/scott-mckenzie.listen: Listen to San Francisco (Be Sure to Wear Some Flowers in Your Hair) and notice the soft accompaniment: the clear little bells and the calm guitar give the song a friendly, almost floating atmosphere.

artiest/scott-storch.text:
Scott Storch is an American producer and songwriter, born in 1973 on Long Island in New York. He grew up in South Florida and Philadelphia. His mother was a singer. He began his career in 1991 as keyboard player of the hip hop group The Roots and contributed to the albums Organix and Do You Want More?!!!??!. He did not enjoy touring. He preferred to work in the studio and became a producer.

His first big hits were You Got Me by The Roots with Erykah Badu and Eve, and the collaboration with Dr. Dre on Still D.R.E. from 1999. He came up with the piano riff for it and co-wrote the song. In the 2000s he made hits for, among others, 50 Cent, Beyoncé, Christina Aguilera, Justin Timberlake, Chris Brown, Nas and Snoop Dogg. He had five number ones in the American Hot 100, including Baby Boy by Beyoncé and Candy Shop by 50 Cent. An addiction to cocaine sent his career into decline, and in 2015 he went bankrupt. Since then he has been working again with, among others, DJ Khaled and The Game.

Storch is known for beats that need very little: a recognisable riff or motif with space around it. In the course he appears in connection with Still D.R.E., where the beat is minimal: a piano riff, drums and otherwise mostly silence.
artiest/scott-storch.listen: Listen to Still D.R.E. and notice the piano riff that keeps coming back, the drums and the silence between the beats. How little does the beat need to stand out?

artiest/scott-walker.text:
Scott Walker, born Noel Scott Engel, was an American-British singer, composer and producer. He was born in 1943 in Hamilton, Ohio, and grew up in several states and later in California. As a child he appeared in Broadway musicals and for a short time he was seen as a teen idol. In Los Angeles he became interested in the Cool Jazz of Stan Kenton and Bill Evans, in European films by Ingmar Bergman and Federico Fellini and in the Beat Generation. As a teenager he worked as a bass guitarist in studios.

With John Walker and Gary Walker he formed the Walker Brothers. They moved to London in 1965, where the group had hits in the mid-1960s, including Make It Easy on Yourself and The Sun Ain't Gonna Shine Anymore, both number 1 in the United Kingdom. After the group split in 1967 he began a solo career with Scott. Strongly influenced by Jacques Brel, on Scott 2, Scott 3 and Scott 4 he made increasingly challenging baroque pop, with grand orchestrations and dark, literary lyrics. Scott 2 reached number one in the United Kingdom.

When 'Til the Band Comes In and Scott 4 failed commercially, records of covers followed that he later disowned. In the 1980s only Climate of Hunter appeared. From Tilt in 1995 his music became dark and avant-garde, via The Drift and Bish Bosch to Soused, a collaboration with the drone metal band Sunn O))). He died in 2019. His recordings from the 1960s were highly valued in the British underground. The BBC called him one of the most enigmatic and influential figures in rock history.
artiest/scott-walker.listen: Listen to The Sun Ain't Gonna Shine Anymore by the Walker Brothers and notice Scott Walker's baritone above the heavy, almost cinematic orchestral accompaniment.

artiest/scottish-chamber-orchestra.text:
The Scottish Chamber Orchestra, abbreviated SCO, is a chamber orchestra from Edinburgh. It was founded in 1974, with Roderick Brydon as its first principal conductor until 1983. It is one of the five national performing companies of Scotland. It plays throughout the country, with annual tours of the Scottish Highlands and islands, and rehearses mainly in the Queen's Hall in Edinburgh, which was opened in 1979 by Queen Elizabeth II. The orchestra appears regularly at the Edinburgh and Aldeburgh festivals and at the Proms.

After Brydon, Jukka-Pekka Saraste, Ivor Bolton, Joseph Swensen and Robin Ticciati, among others, served as principal conductor. Since 2019 that has been Maxim Emelyanychev. Charles Mackerras was conductor laureate until his death in 2010. In 1980 the orchestra recorded all six Brandenburg Concertos with Raymond Leppard for the BBC, and in the years afterwards the recording of Vivaldi's Four Seasons followed. The orchestra also played with Simon Rattle, then a rising young conductor.

The SCO performs classical and new work. It commissioned more than a hundred new pieces, including from Peter Maxwell Davies, James MacMillan and Judith Weir. It recorded for labels including Deutsche Grammophon and Hyperion and works with Linn Records, among other things for Mozart symphonies under Mackerras. The albums in the list, from Mozart and Haydn to Vivaldi and Handel, show what the orchestra is strong at: clear, agile playing in the repertoire for small forces. In 2023 members played at the coronation of Charles III.
artiest/scottish-chamber-orchestra.listen: Listen to The Four Seasons in the 1982 recording and notice the violin solos and how the small orchestra depicts Vivaldi's thunderstorm and birds with short, sharp strokes.

artiest/seal.text:
Seal, in full Seal Henry Olusegun Olumide Adeola Samuel, is a British singer, songwriter and producer, born in 1963 in London to a Nigerian mother and a Brazilian father. He grew up in foster families in Westminster and trained in architecture. In the 1980s he sang in clubs and bars, joined the funk band Push in 1987 and toured Japan and Thailand. After that he travelled alone through India.

His breakthrough came with Killer, a song by the producer Adamski on which he sang and which reached number 1 in the United Kingdom. He signed with ZTT Records and in 1991 released his debut album Seal, produced by Trevor Horn. It included Crazy and Killer. Crazy became an international hit in 1991. In 1992 he won three Brit Awards. The second album, also called Seal, appeared in 1994 and contains Prayer for the Dying and Kiss from a Rose. That last song later became far better known through the film Batman Forever. Human Being, Seal IV, System, Soul and Standards followed, among others. He won two Ivor Novello Awards and four Grammys.

Seal combines a warm, raw voice with pop, soul and dance. His first records show the sound of the producer Trevor Horn, who remained active after the 1980s, including for Seal and the Russian duo t.A.T.u. In the course Seal therefore appears in the story of Horn.
artiest/seal.listen: Listen to Crazy and notice the heavy, danceable beat, the electronic sounds and the powerful, low voice. Can you hear how Trevor Horn's production makes the song sound grand?

artiest/sean-bergin.text:
Sean Bergin was a South African jazz saxophonist and flautist, born in 1948 in Durban. He was also a composer, teacher and bandleader. As a young man he was influenced by the rich South African jazz. While still young he played at the Blue Note Club in Durban, where Black and white musicians performed together in the time of apartheid. He was aware of politics early on: his Black playmate had to go to a different school from him. Later he played in Cape Town with Winston Mankunku Ngozi.

In 1973 he left for London, where he worked with Dudu Pukwana and Chris McGregor, two of the important South African jazz musicians in exile. After a stay in the United States he settled in Amsterdam in 1976. He became a fixture of the scene around the Bimhuis and led jam sessions in the café De Engelbewaarder. In 1986 he began his group MOB, short for My Own Band, with, among others, Tobias Delius, Wolter Wierbos and Han Bennink. With the musicians of his Nansika project he played South African jazz.

He also worked with Mal Waldron, Louis Moholo, Ernst Reijseger, Boi Akih and Miriam Makeba and played in the Trio San Francisco and in groups around Tristan Honsinger. In 2000 he received the VPRO/Boy Edgar Prize. He died in 2012 in Amsterdam. Sean Bergin brought South African jazz to the Netherlands and linked it with the free improvisation of the Amsterdam scene.
artiest/sean-bergin.listen: Listen to Tale of Three City's and notice the saxophone: can you hear the raw, free improvisation of the Amsterdam scene and at the same time the singing melodies of South African jazz?

artiest/seatbelts.text:
Seatbelts is a Japanese band led by the composer and instrumentalist Yoko Kanno. She put the ensemble together in 1998 to play the music for the anime series Cowboy Bebop. The group is international in make-up and consists of a fixed core with many guest musicians. According to the fictional description on the first album, the name comes from the fact that the musicians wear a seat belt during their vigorous jam sessions.

The group played the entire soundtrack of the series and released seven albums and a live DVD in total, beginning with Cowboy Bebop in 1998. The opening track Tank! became the best-known piece. In 2020, during the coronavirus pandemic, the band recorded a new version of The Real Folk Blues virtually to raise money for relief. On a new YouTube channel the project Session Starducks also began, with new performances of, among others, music from Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex and Macross Frontier. For the Netflix live-action series Kanno returned as composer and the Seatbelts played the music.

The repertoire is mainly jazz, but rock, electronic music, funk, blues and orchestral pop also pass by. In this way every episode of the series got its own musical colour. The Seatbelts show that the music for an anime series can be an independent jazz group that is also appreciated outside the picture, and in doing so they reached an audience that otherwise hears little jazz.
artiest/seatbelts.listen: Listen to Tank! and notice the horns, which from the first second come in like a big band full of energy. Note how the rhythm keeps driving and how the solos alternate.

artiest/sebastian-iradier.text:
Sebastián Iradier was a Spanish composer of Basque descent. He was born in 1809 in Lanciego, in the province of Álava. His publisher in Paris advised him to internationalise his name, so that he also became known as Yradier. He had one daughter, Matilde. His name is above all linked to the habanera, a slow, swaying song of Cuban origin.

His best-known work is La Paloma, which he wrote around 1860 after a visit to Cuba. The song became very popular in Spain and in America, especially in Mexico, and made the habanera widely known there. According to Radio UNAM more than a thousand versions of La Paloma have been made. That makes it, alongside Yesterday by The Beatles, one of the most recorded songs in music history.

Another piece of his is El Arreglito, also a habanera. Georges Bizet assumed it was a folk song, took inspiration from the melody and turned it into the aria L'amour est un oiseau rebelle, also known as the Habanera from his opera Carmen. When he discovered his mistake, he put a note about its origin in the score. Iradier himself died unnoticed in 1865 in Vitoria-Gasteiz. His song went on to lead a life of its own, and showed how a melody from the Caribbean world could win a place in Europe and the rest of the world.
artiest/sebastian-iradier.listen: Listen to La Paloma and notice the swaying rhythm that runs beneath the melody. Can you hear how calm and yet danceable it sounds, and how the melody keeps repeating?

artiest/seo-taiji-and-boys.text:
Seo Taiji and Boys was a South Korean group that was active from 1992 to 1996. Singer and producer Seo Taiji formed it after the break-up of his metal band Sinawe, together with the dancers and backing vocalists Yang Hyun-suk and Lee Juno. They experimented with many styles from Western popular music. On 11 April 1992 they made their debut in a talent show on MBC with Nan Arayo. The jury gave them the lowest score, but the song and the debut album became such a success that Korean pop music was never the same afterwards.

Nan Arayo was one of the first Korean rap songs, with new jack swing, rap verses, a pop-style chorus and new dance steps. The second album from 1993 contained Hayeoga, which combined heavy metal and Korean folk music with the taepyeongso, a Korean oboe. The third album moved towards metal and rock, with Dreaming of Bal-Hae and Classroom Idea, a sharp criticism of the education system. The fourth album from 1995 brought Come Back Home, an excursion into gangsta rap, and Pilseung. The song Regret of the Times was banned by an ethics committee because of its criticism of the government. In January 1996 the group stopped, at the height of its popularity. According to Billboard, each of the first three albums sold more than 1.6 million copies.

Seo Taiji and Boys are regarded as the group that changed the Korean pop industry, because they brought rap and social criticism into pop music, despite pressure from censorship committees. In this way they laid the foundation for later K-pop.
artiest/seo-taiji-and-boys.listen: Listen to Come Back Home and notice the high, nasal rap voice and the hard beat. Also notice how quickly the vocals and the music follow one another.

artiest/septeto-nacional-de-ignacio-pine.text:
The Septeto Nacional, in full the Septeto Nacional de Ignacio Piñeiro, was a Cuban group that developed the son, the music style of Cuba, further before Arsenio Rodríguez did so. The group began in 1927 as a sextet in the centre of Havana, under the leadership of Ignacio Piñeiro. The most important innovation was that a trumpet was added to the percussion, the vocals and the stringed instruments. That brought the number of musicians to seven and gave the name septeto its meaning.

In 1929 the group played at the Ibero-American Exposition in Seville. In 1933 it was invited to the world's fair Century of Progress in Chicago. That same year Lázaro Herrera took over the leadership, because Piñeiro left the group for financial reasons. Despite the success the musicians earned very little. In 1937 the group broke up, but in 1940 it came together once more for a recording and later for a television appearance. Later compilations of its work appeared, such as Sones Cubanos and Poetas del son.

The septet's music is son in its classic form: vocals in changing voices, guitar and tres, trumpet and percussion, with a rhythm that dances but does not rush. The sound is one of the building blocks on which salsa was later built. For anyone who wants to understand the history of Latin American pop, this group is an early and important example.
artiest/septeto-nacional-de-ignacio-pine.listen: Listen to Échale Salsita and notice the trumpet, which plays between the vocals and the stringed instruments. Can you hear how the rhythms run through one another and yet together form one light dance?

artiest/sequentia.text:
Sequentia is an early music ensemble, founded in 1977 by Benjamin Bagby and Barbara Thornton. The group came into being in Basel and moved that same year to Cologne, where it worked for more than twenty years. In 2002 it settled in Paris. The group concentrates mainly on medieval music, and in particular on music with text: Gregorian chant and stories with music, such as the Icelandic Edda. Bagby and Thornton did their own research into the projects they performed.

The group's first record is considered to be Ludi Sancti Nicolai from 1978, the recording of two twelfth-century miracle plays about Saint Nicholas, which they staged in 1977. The style was already dramatic and angular, with partly improvised instrumentation. Albums followed such as Ordo virtutum by Hildegard von Bingen, English Songs of the Middle Ages, Motets and Chansons, the series Vox Iberica and Aquitania. The recordings appeared mainly on Deutsche Harmonia Mundi. In 2016 the group performed Songs of Consolation, written by the philosopher Boethius in the year 523, after a stolen eleventh-century manuscript had been recovered.

The core members were Bagby, Thornton, Norbert Rodenkirchen and, after Thornton's death, Katarina Livljanic. The other singers and players are chosen for each project. Sequentia showed that medieval music need not sound stiff, but can be lively, narrative and almost theatrical.
artiest/sequentia.listen: Listen to Garrit gallus / In nova fert and notice the different voices, each singing a text of its own at the same time. Can you hear how the voices cross one another without the line getting lost?

artiest/sergei-rachmaninov.text:
Sergei Rachmaninoff was a Russian composer, virtuoso pianist and conductor. He was born in 1873 into a noble family with a fondness for music and the army. At the age of four he received piano lessons from his mother, and later he studied piano and composition at the Moscow Conservatory, from which he graduated in 1892. He was regarded as one of the best pianists of his time.

In 1897 the premiere of his first symphony was a miserable failure. Rachmaninoff fell into a depression lasting four years and hardly wrote anything, until, thanks to supportive therapy, he completed the Second Piano Concerto in 1901, which was very well received. From 1904 to 1906 he was a conductor at the Bolshoi Theatre, after which he moved to Dresden. In 1909 he made his first tour of the United States. After the Russian Revolution he left Russia for good and settled in New York in 1918. After that he was mainly a concert pianist and wrote only six more works. He died in 1943 in Beverly Hills.

His music is late Romantic, with long, singing melodies, a great deal of feeling, a dense texture and a rich orchestral sound. The piano plays a leading role in his work, as in the piano concertos, the Third Piano Concerto and the Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini. He also wrote the orchestral piece The Isle of the Dead, the Symphony no. 2 and 24 preludes for piano. Rachmaninoff is regarded as one of the last great representatives of Romanticism in Russian classical music. His melodies have also often been borrowed in pop music and film.
artiest/sergei-rachmaninov.listen: Listen to the beginning of the Piano Concerto no. 2: the piano opens alone, with heavy, slowly swelling chords, before the orchestra enters with the great melody.

artiest/sergej-prokofjev.text: Sergei Prokofiev was born in 1891 in what is now Ukraine and studied at the conservatory in Saint Petersburg. After years in the West he returned to the Soviet Union in the 1930s. His first film score, Poruchik Kizhe (1934), belongs to a satire; the suite from it, with the well-known 'Troika', became a concert classic. He worked closely with the director Sergei Eisenstein. For Aleksandr Nevski (1938) they carefully matched image and music to each other; sometimes Prokofiev wrote the music first and Eisenstein edited to it. The Battle on the Ice is the most famous example of this. They also made Ivan Grozny (1944) together. Prokofiev himself turned Nevski into a cantata.
artiest/sergej-prokofjev.listen: Notice how chorus, brass and percussion in the Battle on the Ice build a movement from silence to chaos, exactly to the rhythm of the editing.

artiest/sex-pistols.text:
The Sex Pistols were formed in London in 1975 by guitarist Steve Jones, drummer Paul Cook and bassist Glen Matlock, with singer John Lydon, who called himself Johnny Rotten. The manager was Malcolm McLaren, who ran the clothes shop SEX on King's Road with the designer Vivienne Westwood. The Sex Pistols existed for less than three years, but became the face of British punk: short, hard songs as an answer to the big, complicated rock of the 1970s.

In October 1976 the band signed to EMI. On 26 November Anarchy in the UK was released, produced by Chris Thomas. He layered Jones's guitar parts on top of one another many times, so that a wall of guitar sound arose. The single did not climb higher than number 38. After a TV interview with the presenter Bill Grundy, in which the band members swore, EMI dropped the group in January 1977. Sid Vicious replaced Matlock in early 1977. God Save the Queen was released during the silver jubilee of Queen Elizabeth II. The BBC and almost all commercial stations refused to play it, but it still entered the chart at number 2. The only studio album, Never Mind the Bollocks (October 1977), reached number 1 in England.

In January 1978 Rotten announced the end of the band from a stage in San Francisco. Vicious died in 1979 of a heroin overdose. After a Sex Pistols concert in that city, Bernard Sumner and Peter Hook formed Joy Division. In 2006 the band was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, but refused to attend.
artiest/sex-pistols.listen: In Anarchy in the UK (1976) Steve Jones's guitar sounds like a wall. That is because producer Chris Thomas recorded the same part many times on top of itself. Notice how above it Rotten does not sing but sneers.

artiest/shabaka-and-the-ancestors.text:
Shabaka and the Ancestors is the band of the British saxophonist, composer and bandleader Shabaka Hutchings. He was born in 1984 in London and grew up in Barbados, where at the age of nine he began playing the clarinet, among other things to the rhymes of Nas and Tupac. Back in England he studied clarinet at the Guildhall School of Music and Drama. In London he ended up in the Tomorrow's Warriors programme, where he met many of his later fellow players in the South London jazz scene.

The Ancestors made their debut in 2016 with the album Wisdom of Elders on Gilles Peterson's label Brownswood Recordings. In 2020 We Are Sent Here by History appeared on Impulse! Records. Hutchings also played in Sons of Kemet and The Comet Is Coming, two other groups that helped bring British jazz to a wider audience. In 2018 he curated part of the programme of the Dutch festival Le Guess Who?. In 2020 he also started the label Native Rebel Recordings.

Many young London musicians set the label jazz aside, because their influences range from acid house and drum and bass to hip hop and soca, with less blues than in American jazz. Hutchings too worked with, among others, the Sun Ra Arkestra and Mulatu Astatke. At the end of 2023 he announced that he was taking a break from playing the saxophone. The Ancestors show how jazz sounds in the London of today.
artiest/shabaka-and-the-ancestors.listen: Listen to a track from We Are Sent Here by History and notice the interplay between the saxophone and the rhythmic interplay of the whole band beneath it.

artiest/shabaka-hutchings.text: The saxophonist and clarinettist Shabaka Hutchings was born in London and grew up in Barbados, where he heard calypso and reggae. Back in England he studied the clarinet and entered jazz through Tomorrow's Warriors. He led three groups at the same time: Sons of Kemet, with tuba and two drummers; The Comet Is Coming, with electronics; and Shabaka and the Ancestors, with South African musicians. His music often deals with Black history and identity. In 2023 he stopped playing the saxophone in order to concentrate on flutes, including the Japanese shakuhachi.
artiest/shabaka-hutchings.listen: Hear the tuba and two drummers beneath the saxophone: jazz as dance music.

artiest/shabba-ranks.text:
Shabba Ranks, born Rexton Gordon in 1966, is a Jamaican dancehall musician. He was born in Sturge Town in Saint Ann and grew up in Seaview Gardens in Kingston. He became known for toasting, that is, rapping over a rhythm, and less for singing. He was a protégé of the DJ Josey Wales and at first performed as Co-Pilot. His international career began in the late 1980s, and in 1989 he signed with Epic Records.

His breakthrough in North America came with the album Just Reality from 1990. The albums As Raw as Ever and X-tra Naked won a Grammy for best reggae album in 1992 and 1993. His biggest hit outside Jamaica was Mr. Loverman, a reggae fusion that was played worldwide. Other well-known titles are Housecall with Maxi Priest, Slow and Sexy with Johnny Gill and Ting A Ling. He also worked with Chuck Berry and rappers such as KRS-One and Chubb Rock, and in 1993 he contributed a rap and reggae version of Family Affair to the soundtrack of Addams Family Values. In 1996 Epic dropped him. Later he resurfaced with Busta Rhymes and other artists.

The song Dem Bow from Just Reality, produced by Bobby Digital Dixon, had a rhythm that became so popular in Puerto Rico that early reggaeton was simply called dembow. That rhythm is still the hallmark of reggaeton. Ranks was also criticised for his statements about homosexuals and for a lyric containing violence against them. His music nevertheless remained influential for dancehall, reggae and hip hop.
artiest/shabba-ranks.listen: Listen to Mr. Loverman and notice Ranks's sing-jay delivery: he raps and sings over a rhythm that sounds calm, yet emphatic. Hear how the chorus sticks in your head.

artiest/shakti.text:
Shakti was a fusion band, founded by the English guitarist John McLaughlin and the Indian violinist L. Shankar, with Zakir Hussain on tabla and Vikku Vinayakram on ghatam. The group began in 1973 under the name Turiyananda Sangit, a name from Sri Chinmoy that means something like the peak of delight in music. Later it changed this to Shakti, which means creative intelligence, beauty and power, because the members wanted a name that Western listeners could identify with. The group came together after the break-up of the first Mahavishnu Orchestra and toured extensively from 1975 to 1977. Albums from that time are A Handful of Beauty and Natural Elements from 1977.

Shakti played acoustic fusion music that combined the Carnatic music of South India with jazz. Elements of Celtic folk music and classical music also played a role. The band also brought together the Hindustani music of the north and the Carnatic tradition of the south: Hussain came from the north, Shankar and Vikku from the south. Two performances at the Montreux Jazz Festival, in 1976 and 1977, are on McLaughlin's box set Montreux Concerts.

Between 1982 and 1984 the group came together for tours in India. In 1997 McLaughlin and Hussain formed Remember Shakti. In 2020 the band reunited and in 2023 This Moment appeared, the first album under that name in 46 years, which received a Grammy in 2024 for Best Global Music Album. Shakti showed that Indian and Western improvisation can find each other.
artiest/shakti.listen: Listen to a track from A Handful of Beauty and notice the conversation between acoustic guitar, violin and the fast tabla and ghatam. Can you hear how they take over one another's patterns?

artiest/shankar-jaikishan.text:
Shankar-Jaikishan, S-J for short, was an Indian composer duo from the Hindi film industry. It consisted of Shankar Singh Ram Singh Raghuvanshi, born in 1922 in Hyderabad, and Jaikishan Dayabhai Panchal, born in 1929 in Gujarat. Shankar played the tabla and at the Prithvi Theatre also learned the sitar, accordion and piano. Jaikishan was a harmonium player. They met at the Prithvi Theatre in Mumbai, where they both worked, and quickly became friends. Through that theatre they came into contact with Raj Kapoor.

Their career began in 1949 with Raj Kapoor's romantic drama Barsaat. From 1949 to 1971 they wrote the music for 136 films, including Awāra in 1951, Shree 420 in 1955 and Junglee in 1961. They worked with singers such as Mukesh, Mohammed Rafi, Lata Mangeshkar and Asha Bhosle and often with the lyricists Shailendra and Hasrat Jaipuri. After Jaikishan's death in 1971 Shankar went on making music for 43 more films, under the name Shankar-Jaikishan.

Their work was often based on ragas and combined melodic charm with a rich orchestral sound. In this way they brought film music to a new level of orchestral fullness. They are generally regarded as the greatest composers of the Hindi film industry. Their songs are still popular in India and beyond and strongly influenced the next generation of film composers. The duo belongs to what is often called the golden age of Hindi film music.
artiest/shankar-jaikishan.listen: Listen to a song from Awāra or Shree 420 and notice the orchestral sound: large string parts following a melody built on a raga.

artiest/shanks-en-bigfoot.text:
Shanks & Bigfoot was a British duo of UK garage producers, Steven Meade and Danny Langsman. They began in the late 1990s under the name Doolally and in 1998 made the pirate radio anthem Straight from the Heart. On its first release the song reached number twenty in the British chart. Because of legal problems they had to choose another name, after which they carried on as Shanks & Bigfoot. Straight from the Heart was re-released in 1999, after the success of their big hit, and then reached number nine.

That hit was Sweet Like Chocolate from 1999, with vocals by Sharon Woolf, who had also sung Straight from the Heart. The song had been played in clubs for months before it was released and went straight to number one in the United Kingdom for two weeks. It became one of the most popular singles of the late 1990s. The computer animation that accompanied the song, about a girl in a world of chocolate, was just as well known at the time and was nominated for a BRIT and a MOBO. At the 1999 MOBO Awards the duo won the prize for best British dance act. A bidding war for the duo followed, and they eventually signed with Zomba Records. In 2000 their only album came out, Swings & Roundabouts, with vocals by Terri Walker, and the single Sing-A-Long.

The music is 2step, a light, syncopated form of garage with a smooth bass line and a soulful vocal part. The duo belonged to the wave that defined British dance music around 2000 and showed that garage could also reach the pop charts.
artiest/shanks-en-bigfoot.listen: Listen to Sweet Like Chocolate and notice the rhythm, which keeps falling slightly off-kilter, and the supple bass. Can you hear how the voice lies clear and soft on top of it?

artiest/shara-nelson.text:
Shara Nelson is an English singer and songwriter, born in 1965. Her first record was the 1983 single Aiming at Your Heart, under the name Shara Nelson & The Circuit. In 1986 her first solo single, Can't Get Over You, appeared under the name Shara. In the late 1980s she began working with The Wild Bunch, the Bristol DJ and production collective from which Massive Attack emerged.

With Massive Attack she released the single Daydreaming in 1990. She did not only sing, but also co-wrote songs, such as Unfinished Sympathy, which appeared in 1991 on the debut album Blue Lines. The single reached number thirteen in the British chart and is ranked highly in lists by, among others, MTV2 and NME. In 1993 she began a solo career again with Down That Road, followed by the album What Silence Knows. That album was shortlisted for the 1994 Mercury Prize, and she was nominated for two Brit Awards. The second album, Friendly Fire, appeared in 1995. Later she worked with, among others, Charles Webster and Air Cuba.

Her voice is warm and sensitive, and she fits well with the slow, dark trip-hop of Bristol. In the course she appears in the chapter on the jazz festivals, as the voice in Unfinished Sympathy: a string orchestra over a hip hop beat.
artiest/shara-nelson.listen: Listen to Unfinished Sympathy and notice the strings above the hip hop beat. How does Shara Nelson's voice make the song grow from intimate to grand?

artiest/sharon-den-adel.text:
Sharon den Adel is a Dutch singer and songwriter, the lead singer of the symphonic metal band Within Temptation. She was born in 1974 in Waddinxveen and as a child lived in Indonesia for five years. The Balinese dancers she saw there later inspired her movements on stage. From the age of fourteen she performed with various bands, including the blues rock band Kashiro. She has a bachelor's degree in fashion design and worked for a fashion company, until the success of the single Ice Queen came.

In 1996 she founded Within Temptation with her partner Robert Westerholt, at first under the name The Portal. She has never had formal singing lessons, but sings as a mezzo-soprano and practised alone for years, three or four hours a day. Her parents played Pink Floyd, Queen, Santana and Kate Bush. Later she was gripped by Nirvana, Tori Amos and the gothic metal of Paradise Lost, which Westerholt and she cite as an important influence for the combination of growls, heavy guitars and a clear, operatic female voice. She calls the band's work epic and cinematic.

Besides the band she makes solo work under the name My Indigo, which sounds more intimate. She designs her own stage costumes and the band's merchandise. In 2018 she was the Dutch chair of the jury for the Eurovision Song Contest. Her voice is among the most recognisable in Dutch rock and metal.
artiest/sharon-den-adel.listen: Listen to Ice Queen by Within Temptation and notice Sharon den Adel's voice: she sings clearly and powerfully above heavy guitars and orchestral sounds.

artiest/shellback.text:
Shellback, real name Karl Johan Schuster, is a Swedish producer and songwriter, born in 1985. He began as a guitarist in the metal band Blinded Colony and as a teenager hardly listened to pop. At sixteen he came into contact with Max Martin through an acquaintance, and Martin wondered what pop music by this metal musician would sound like. In 2006 Martin invited him to his studio in Stockholm, and since 2007 Schuster has been under contract to Martin's company Maratone.

Among his first songs with Martin are So What by Pink from 2008 and If U Seek Amy by Britney Spears. In 2012 he topped Billboard's year-end list of producers and won the STIM Platinum guitar prize. Together with Martin he worked for, among others, Taylor Swift, Adam Lambert, Usher, Avril Lavigne, Ariana Grande, Adele and Maroon 5. With Swift he made the album 1989 from 2014. He also wrote and produced Can't Stop the Feeling! for the film Trolls, together with Martin and Justin Timberlake. In 2015 he made arrangements for the album Freedom by the Swedish band Refused. He won four Grammys.

His style is energetic and percussive, with a rock and metal background beneath the pop. In the course he is the Swedish producer with whom Swift made the move from country to pop on 1989, as part of the modern hit factory.
artiest/shellback.listen: Listen to Shake It Off by Taylor Swift and notice the driving drums and the short, conversational lines. How does this sound as a song built mainly for the chorus?
